title: Using Vertically Aligned Carbon Nanofiber Arrays on Rigid or Flexible Substrates for Delivery of Biomolecules and Dyes to Plants
protocol: Spincoat a silicon wafer with PMMA 495 A4 resist at 4000 rpm.
Bake the wafer at 180 °C for 5 min.
Allow the wafer to cool for 10 s.
Spincoat a second layer of PMMA 950 A2 and bake it at 180 °C for 5 min.
Use electron beam lithography to define catalyst dots with diameters of 300 nm, spaced at a pitch of 10 µm or 35 µm in arrays measuring 3 mm x 3 mm.
Develop the resist in 1:3 methyl-isobutyl ketone: IPA for 1.5 min.
Rinse the wafer with IPA and dry it with N2.
Check for the array of dots using a brightfield microscope (20x objective).
Clean the wafer of residual resist with oxygen plasma exposure for 6 s.
Deposit an adhesive layer of Ti or Cr, 10 nm thick, via electron beam evaporation.
Deposit a Ni catalyst layer, 130 nm or 150 nm thick, under conditions of current below 0.2 A at 10 kV, pressure below 5 x 10-6 Torr, and deposition rate at ~1 A/s for line-of-sight deposition.
Use sequential bath sonication to remove the metal deposited on the underlying resist layer, leaving only Ni directly on the silicon wafer in the defined dot pattern.
Prepare 3 containers with acetone.
Bath sonicate the wafer in acetone for 1 min at room temperature (RT, 20 °C) at a frequency of 35 kHz.
Repeat sonication with acetone two more times.
Rinse the wafer with IPA after each sonication cycle.
Dry the wafer with N2 gas after rinsing.
Check the geometry of catalyst shape using scanning electron microscopy (SEM).
Tilt the SEM stage to a 30° angle for imaging.
Use a voltage of 1-3 kV and a beam current of ~100 pA for SEM imaging.
Maintain a working distance of ~5 mm during SEM imaging.
Quarter the silicon wafer.
Place the quartered silicon wafer in the direct current plasma enhanced chemical vapor deposition chamber (dc-PECVD).
Optimize growth parameters to control the length and taper of nanofibers, ensuring tips are less than 200 nm.
Use a current of 1-1.5 A and a voltage range of 440-560 V during fiber growth.
Implement a pre-treatment phase with ammonia flow while heating the machine and substrate to 620 °C.
Turn on the carbon source (acetylene) 10 seconds before starting the plasma.
Use Ni catalyst thicknesses between 130 nm and 150 nm, depending on desired fiber characteristics.
For a Ni thickness of 130 nm, use a current of 1.75 A and growth time of 70 minutes with an acetylene : ammonia ratio of 45 sccm : 100 sccm.
For a Ni thickness of 150 nm, use a current of 1.5 A and growth time of 80 minutes with an acetylene : ammonia ratio of 48 sccm : 100 sccm.
Maintain a growth temperature of 620 °C and pressure of 10 torr during plasma for all fiber growths.
Ensure the shower head height is set to 20 mm for all fiber growths.
Assess the geometry of resulting fibers using SEM at a 30° tilt with an acceleration potential of 1 kV.
Spincoat a layer of photoresist (SPR955) onto the fibers at 1000 rpm for 45 s.
Dice the ¼ wafer into 3 mm x 3 mm arrays using a dicing saw.
Spincoat SU-8 2015 photoresist onto the wafers or quarter wafers at 4000 rpm for 45 s.
Softbake the wafer for 3 min at 95 °C.
Expose the wafer with a 3 mm x 3 mm array patterned mask that aligns with the defined pattern from electron beam lithography at 95 mJ/cm2.
Perform a post-exposure bake for 6 min at 95 °C.
Develop the wafer in SU-8 developer for 15 s.
Rinse the wafer with IPA.
Dry the wafer with N2, moving from top to bottom.
Spincoat patterned wafers with a protective layer of thin photoresist (SPR 955 CM 0.7) at 3000 rpm for 45 s and softbake for 30 s at 90 °C.
Deposit a thin silicon oxide layer to the wafer (2-3 nm) by placing it in an atomic layer deposition for 22 cycles at 100 °C.
Use a dicing saw to cut the wafer into 3 mm x 3 mm squares.
Align the dicing saw to the preexisting pattern on the wafer.
Assess the geometry of the resulting fibers using SEM at a 30° tilt with an acceleration potential of 3 kV.
Store chips in the dark if storing for long-term use (>1 week).
Place individual chips in acetone for 30 min or until the SU-8 starts to curl to separate flexible substrates from rigid substrates.
Wash SU-8 films (either attached to or detached from rigid substrates) with IPA for 5 min and then with water for 5 min.
Place the chips in a commercial box with a sticky pad when transporting them.
Transfer the SU-8 film using tweezers, placing it on water-soluble tape or on top of thin silicone rubber with a thin PET backing (12.5 µm thick).
Press on the edges of the SU-8 square to help it stick to the tape/silicone rubber-PET.
Use the VACNF films immediately after preparation for immediate use.
Mix the two parts of a 2-part kit for silicone rubber together (the elastomer and the crosslinker).
Cut out a square of PET and tape it down in a clear plastic dish.
Pour a very thin layer of silicone rubber on top of the PET.
Cure the silicone rubber at 80 °C for 1-2 h.
Remove photoresist with increment washes of acetone (100%, 5 min), IPA (100%, 5 min), and ddH2O (5 min) prior to use.
Place the plant tissue to be impaled on a hard surface for support.
Place a 1 µL droplet of dye or DNA (200 ng) onto the surface of the plant tissue.
Place a VACNF chip with a rigid substrate on top of the droplet, orienting the fibers such that they will come into contact with the droplet.
Tap the chip gently using the flat side of a pair of tweezers.
Mark the area of the plant that the chip came into contact with using a soft-tipped marker.
Remove the VACNF chips after delivery.
Remove the photoresist from VACNF chips with increment washes of acetone (100%, 5 min), IPA (100%, 5 min), and ddH2O (5 min).
Drop cast 1 μL droplet of dye or plasmid DNA (200 ng) onto the fiber side of VACNF chip with rigid substrate.
Ensure to place the droplet in the center of the chip and cover several fibers.
Let the droplet dry for 15 min.
Position the VACNF chip such that the fiber side contacts the plant tissue.
Tap the chip gently with tweezers to secure it onto the tissue.
Place 1 µL droplet of dye or DNA (200 ng) on the fiber side of the SU-8 film.
Let the droplet dry for 10 minutes in the center of the chip.
Use sharp tweezers to place the VACNF film onto the plant surface.
Gently roll a small makeup applicator over the VACNF film.
Mark areas where flexible substrates are placed with a soft-tipped marker.
Remove the flexible substrates from the plant surface using tape.
Practice applying the VACNF films prior to conducting biomolecule or dye delivery.
Repeat steps for controls and store plants as mentioned in step 3.7 of the on-plant method.
Image samples using a confocal microscope with emission and excitation wavelengths suitable for the delivered fluorescent probe/reporter.
Capture at least 5 images for each sample.
Measure fluorescence values as total fluorescence (integrated density) in 20 µm x 20 µm confocal image areas using ImageJ.
